title: Ground Loop — Editor Intro
summary: Opening splash frames communications as a physical engineering problem: a distributed network has to remain useful through distance, noise, dust, old equipment and interference.
panelPlan: Full-page opening/title splash across a busy but ordinary Mojave service yard: rugged radios, paper routes, a relay box, old pump or vehicle electrical hardware and long desert distance all coexist in one working environment.
Use visual interference—dust, cable runs, motor housings, weak line-of-sight and distant terrain—without turning it into glowing cyberpunk signal graphics.
Do not show the exact duplicate dispatch, pump-start relay failure, hydroelectric gallery, rebuilt switch, seized relay cabinet or any later Issue 6 result.
The typography should make THE PHYSICAL WORLD IS ALREADY VERY GOOD AT BREAKING NETWORKS the central pressure, with the title as the answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: It has no guarantee that two places will hear the same thing at the same time.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Mojave is full of distance, dust, old motors, bad grounds, weak radios and roads that turn a few minutes into a few hours.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The physical world is already very good at breaking networks.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: This time, Launch-Shop has to build for the ugly version.

directionInline.text: Non-diegetic opening title page. Preserve exact caption text. Promise physical resilience without pre-solving it. Do not show any specific Issue 6 failure or workaround beyond the established fact that Public Sky now depends on imperfect communications across the Mojave.
